title: Japji 8–15, whole
tomorrow: after listening and trusting, the Japji starts to count. count what?

cards: A chorus at a game, a refrain at a wedding: after the second time, you know where it's going before it lands. Pauri eight of the Japji does that. Suniai, it begins: by listening.
Pauri nine: suniai. Ten: suniai. Eleven: suniai.
Then the word changes, and the next four begin mannai: by trusting. So, one question for today: why does listening come first?

teach.b: The suniai pauris pile up what listening does: by listening, the adepts and the holy came to be; by listening, the blind find the way.
Each one ends on the same refrain: Nanak bhagataa sadaa vigaas, suniai dookh paap kaa naas. The devotees are always in bloom; by listening, pain and wrong are gone.
Then the mannai pauris turn to what comes after hearing: trusting, taking it in. Guru Nanak says the state of the one who trusts can't be told; there's no paper or pen for it.
By trusting, awareness wakes; the path opens; the door of freedom is found. So the Japji's answer comes in an order: listen, then trust. Now a neighbor, in its own words.
Paul, writing to the Christians in Rome, says something that rhymes.
In the King James Bible: "So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God."
Shared ground: trust doesn't start with effort; it starts with the ears. And one honest difference. Paul means hearing the message about Christ, preached and believed.
Guru Nanak means listening to the Name itself, a listening that changes the listener, and a trust he says no words can reach.

how: Sikhs reciting the Japji in the morning move through the suniai and mannai pauris in order; in some gurdwara classes they are taught as a pair, listening and then trusting.

games.q: a classmate says, 'just trust, don't overthink it.' what order do pauris eight to fifteen give?
o: listen first, then trust: four suniai pauris come before the four mannai.
trust first, then listen; you only hear clearly once you believe.
no order: listening and trusting are the same word in Gurmukhi.
games.why: suniai, by listening, opens pauris eight to eleven; mannai, by trusting, opens twelve to fifteen. hearing first, then the yes.

practice: Close your eyes and choose one sound in the room: a fan, the traffic, your own breath. Just listen to it, without naming it or judging it. When your mind wanders off, come back to the listening, as many times as it takes.

wordCard.voice: Japji 8. Pauris eight to fifteen, read whole: four that begin suniai, by listening, and four that begin mannai, by trusting.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: by listening. it opens Japji pauris eight to eleven.

carryVoice: For the road: listen, trust, in that order, the ears first and then the yes. Three of the summit.
